key_insight: A homozygous founder RAG1 p.C176F variant in Old Order Mennonites causes a highly variable partial RAG deficiency, where intrinsic hypomorphic recombination defects combine with extrinsic immune pressures to drive diverse clinical and immune phenotypes.
clinical_relevance: Multi-omic biomarkers such as CMV-specific immune decline, IFN-related signatures, and skewed B/T cell repertoires may help monitor disease progression and identify patients who could benefit from timely hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
method: Studied 18 Old Order Mennonite individuals with a shared novel RAG1 founder variant.
Measured recombinase activity, immune cell phenotypes, cytokine/chemokine markers, and antibody signatures.
Profiled BCR and TCR repertoires to link intrinsic and extrinsic drivers of disease.
evidence_signal: The cohort showed only 25.8% of wild-type recombinase activity, with clinically diverse outcomes that correlated with CMV competence loss, anti-IFN antibodies, elevated CXCL9/10, and repertoire changes.
watch_item: This is a rare founder cohort, so findings may not generalize broadly and biomarker-guided treatment decisions still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Multi-omics approach to map a clinically diverse large cohort with homozygous founder RAG1 p.C176F variant among Old Order Mennonites
